land.text: the Crown's Ulster, granted to Walter de Burgh in 1263; the page also records an earlier title granted to John de Courcy in 1181

predecessors.note: The legal predecessor is the Lordship of Ireland under the English Crown (eu-11-x); Cliopatria's seed lists the earldom as a member of the (Kingdom of England) umbrella in 1326-1332.

land.text: 'By the 15th century the earldom was restricted to coastal enclaves' in Down and around Carrickfergus; the title of Earl of Ulster 'passed to the Crown in 1461'

successors.note: Most of the land went to no state: the Magennis clan took some 'following its collapse in 1333' and the Uí Néill rose in Ulster. Cliopatria carries the same Antrim and Down polygon for 1333-1351 under the Earldom of Desmond (a row mix-up, see the desmond dossier).

capitals.name: Carrickfergus
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Carrickfergus Castle', the earldom's capital and de Courcy's administrative centre.

correction.text: most of what are now County Antrim and County Down

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1263-1325, which Cliopatria lacks: 'Walter de Burgh: Granted the earldom in 1263' and the earldom 'covered most of what are now County Antrim and County Down, and briefly reached west to Lough Foyle'. Antrim and Down are the 15 Northern Ireland districts named here (about 6,800 km2 on the grid); the Lough Foyle reach is undated and not drawn.

correction.text: most of what are now County Antrim and County Down; the years run to June 1333 (William Donn de Burgh killed 'in June 1333')

keyframe_review.note: 2,333 km2 on seven cells (the east coast strip around Belfast Lough and Carrickfergus) against the page's 'most of what are now County Antrim and County Down' (about 6,800 km2 on the grid): ratio 0.35, beyond a factor of two, so the shape is too small and the page's land is used. William Donn de Burgh was Earl of Ulster from 1326 to 1333 (infobox '1326-1333'), so the shape should run to June 1333 rather than stop in 1332. The infobox of the Earldom page gives no area.

region.text: most of what are now County Antrim and County Down

ledger.note: 1263: Walter de Burgh is granted the earldom of Ulster. 'Walter de Burgh: Granted the earldom in 1263'; the page's older title, earl palatine granted to John de Courcy in 1181 by Henry II, is the first creation. The capital is Carrickfergus Castle; the land is 'most of what are now County Antrim and County Down'.

region.text: the earldom's Antrim and Down, 'following its collapse in 1333'

ledger.note: 1333: the earldom collapses with the murder of William Donn de Burgh. 'In June 1333, he was killed by de Mandeville, Sir John de Logan, and others' and his de Burgh kinsmen 'began the Burke Civil War for supremacy'; the Earldom page dates the 'collapse in 1333', after which the Magennis clan took over some lands and by the 15th century only coastal enclaves in Down and around Carrickfergus were left. The title passed to the Crown in 1461.

wars.name: Bruce invasion of Ulster
wars.outcome: Peace 'ended with a siege of Carrickfergus Castle by Edward Bruce in 1315'; the campaign of the 1310s caused 'heavy damage from which the earldom never recovered'. The page gives no further dates.
wars.note: The page gives only the siege of 1315; the end of the invasion is not on any page opened.

wars.name: Burke Civil War
wars.outcome: After William Donn was killed in June 1333 his de Burgh kinsmen 'began the Burke Civil War for supremacy' (William had had his cousin Sir Walter Liath de Burgh starved to death at Greencastle, near the mouth of Lough Foyle, in February 1332).
wars.note: The Burke Civil War's end is not on the pages opened (the page gives no dates).

certainty.note: A feudal earldom whose extent is described only as 'most of' Antrim and Down, briefly west to Lough Foyle; no survey or treaty line.

sources.title: Earldom of Ulster
sources.note: Created 1181 (de Courcy), Walter de Burgh 1263, capital Carrickfergus, extent Antrim and Down, Bruce's siege 1315, collapse 1333, Crown 1461.

notes:
Written by eu-11-j on 2026-10-25 from two pages (budget 1-2).

Life span: Cliopatria has one shape for 1326-1332. The dossier starts in 1263 (Walter de Burgh's grant, Earldom page) with a new keyframe for 1263-1325, and ends in June 1333 with the murder of William Donn de Burgh and the 'collapse in 1333'. This overlaps the Kingdom of England / Lordship of Ireland shapes drawn by other groups; the earldom is the (Kingdom of England) umbrella member in Cliopatria. The older title of John de Courcy (1181) is not given a keyframe.
The Cliopatria shape (2,333 km2) is too small for the page's description (ratio 0.35); the corrected region is the 15 Northern Ireland districts of Antrim and Down.
Cliopatria's Earldom of Desmond shape for 1333-1351 is this same Antrim and Down polygon (see earldom-of-desmond.json, verdict 'wrong'). After June 1333 the pages give no state for the land: the Magennis clan, the Uí Néill (O'Neill) and the Burke Civil War; the enclaves around Carrickfergus and Down stayed English. A gap-filler should open 'Gaelic resurgence' or 'Lordship of Ireland', and the Bruce invasion article for 1315-1318 (the First War of Scottish Independence page does not mention Ireland). The Bruce campaign's end, the Battle of Faughart, the 1328 coming of age and the Red Earl's dates are not on the two pages and are not recorded.
Pages disagree: William Donn's birth is 17 September or 13 September 1312; no consequence for the map.
Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-england (the Crown), a Lordship of Ireland (eu-11-x), Magennis and O'Neill (Gaelic lordships; not Cliopatria rows), the Connacht Burkes. No new region names needed (Northern Ireland districts exist in admin1).
